result.answer: Only partly. The failed message said the patient moved to WARD-B, bed BAY2-04, at 09:20 UTC. That is no longer where the patient is. A later transfer to WARD-C, bed BAY1-07, at 09:45 UTC reached the demo patient records system (Records Out). It now shows the patient admitted on WARD-C at version 2. So the WARD-B transfer no longer holds as the patient's current place. Resending it could move the patient back to a ward they have already left. What still holds is the fact that the WARD-B stay happened. It matters only because Records Out keeps a complete movement history, and that history goes straight from WARD-A to WARD-C. If Records Out only needed the current placement, the setting would be 'current_state' instead of 'history_of_record' (W1). This case would then close with nothing to send and no escalation, because WARD-C is already correct. One more point: the alternative's wording talks about cancelling the later transfer and replaying both. The correction steps do not do that. They keep WARD-C and add WARD-B as a past movement. From this perspective, keeping WARD-C as the current place is right.
